proposed_from.topic: Censoring-robust spectral synthetic survival control under covariate-dependent right censoring. Fix N0 donor units, T0 pre-treatment times, J post-treatment grid points and rank r while K independent individuals per cell tends to infinity; assume conditional independent censoring given covariates with positivity, exact donor-span transport, a rank-r singular gap, cross-fitted censor and event-survival nuisances with product rate o(K^-1/2), and nondegenerate covariance. Construct augmented-IPCW cell survival estimates, differentiate the full stacked rank-r pseudoinverse map, and prove joint root-K asymptotic linearity, a Gaussian-multiplier simultaneous band for the J-point untreated counterfactual curve, a studentized grid-RMST effect interval, and an open-subclass theorem that unadjusted KM/PCR has fixed bias. Consumer: Han and Shah's 925-patient, 10-country TCL analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For donor-pre matrix M, target row y, donor-post matrix B, and P=M_r^+, the presolver derived the full differential D(yPB)=h_yPB+y[-PHP+PP' H'(I-MP)+(I-PM)H'P'P]B+yPh_B. The rational rank-two witness has det(M)=-3/25, weights (1/2,1/2), counterfactual curve (3/5,3/10), and an informative-censoring construction whose naive KM/PCR limit differs by (1/46560,-2209/124650432). Checks covered censor-positivity failure, singular-gap closure, covariance degeneracy, transport failure, growing grids, full rank, continuous-versus-grid RMST, generic delta-method collapse, and the visible literature without finding a collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: For one fully specified right-censoring AIPCW score and tie convention, prove the joint cellwise cross-fitted expansion with o_p(K^-1/2) remainder and L2-consistent estimated influence vectors from positivity, the common moment bound, nuisance consistency, and a_K b_K=o(K^-1/2), adding any event-survival tail condition actually needed. EARLY KILL TEST: Derive that score's cross-fitted second-order remainder and verify it is O_p(a_K b_K)+o_p(K^-1/2) jointly over all fixed cells and times; if any uncancelled first-order nuisance term survives, pivot or stop. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_ipcw_spectral_ssc_inference.md.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The exact unoccupied object is the joint influence vector obtained by feeding one fully specified cross-fitted survival score into every target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and factual-post cell and applying the full derivative of \(yM_r^+B\). Han and Shah do not permit covariate-dependent censoring or give an asymptotic law; Westling et al. have no learned spectral transport; Agarwal, Shah, and Shen have no censoring nuisance or influence-function inference. The accompanying Kaplan--Meier/PCR proposition is not the classical observation that Kaplan--Meier can be inconsistent: it derives the complete three-block pseudo-limit, verifies an explicit rational nonzero point, and proves a relatively open nonzero-bias subclass. Fan and Liao and Choi, Kwon, and Liao are treated as high-dimensional technique ancestors for the open weak-gap question, not as results extended by the fixed-grid theorem.

seed_details.seed: Orthogonal fixed-grid spectral survival-control limit law with simultaneous inference
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2511.14133, Introduction, Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Appendix E, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Han and Shah identify the untreated post-period survival trajectory by donor-span transport and estimate it by Kaplan--Meier followed by rank-truncated principal-component regression. Their proof first controls cellwise Kaplan--Meier errors, then invokes spectral stability and row-space transport. The conclusion explicitly leaves inverse-probability censoring weighting and covariate incorporation for later work.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the first Kaplan--Meier concentration step by a joint cross-fitted augmented-IPCW expansion, then differentiate all three noisy blocks in \(yM_r^+B\), including both projector corrections in the pseudoinverse derivative.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for synthetic survival control with IPCW, dependent censoring, influence functions, or simultaneous bands returned Han and Shah and generic survival estimators, but no paper composing an orthogonal cell score with the full spectral map.
adjacent_threads: Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024), Theorems 1--2 and Lemmas 4--7: the explicit orthogonal survival score, product remainder, and feasible influence process.
Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025), Theorem 2 and Corollary 2: minimum-norm PCR and row-space out-of-sample transport without censoring-aware inference.
Golub and Pereyra (1973), equation (4.12): the locally constant-rank pseudoinverse differential with both projector corrections.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013): Gaussian multiplier approximation and anti-concentration for maxima.
seed_details.novelty_check: The four threads settle the cell score, deterministic row-space transport, matrix differential, and multiplier calibration separately. None contains the joint influence vector for a survival score propagated through all three learned blocks, so no closer paper subsumes the kernel.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is immediate from Westling et al. and an ordinary delta method.
seed_details.rebuttal: Westling et al. treat one survival law; the new influence vector must preserve within-cell covariance and propagate target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post errors through a rank-truncated pseudoinverse whose two subspace-motion terms are absent from a plug-in weight calculation.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit law is the kernel, not a generic application claim; the score, tie convention, full differential, covariance estimator, band, and grid-RMST contrast are explicit, while the weak-gap regime remains openly posed.

seed_details.seed: Shrinking singular-gap and rank-selection phase transition for spectral survival control
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2311.16440, Introduction, diversified-projection construction, Theorem 3.1, bias-correction discussion, and concluding applications.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Choi, Kwon, and Liao replace consistent rank recovery by diversified projections and explicitly correct the ridge-type bias created by rank overestimation. Their feasible central limit theorem concerns linear functionals of a high-dimensional low-rank matrix, not a fixed-panel nonlinear pseudoinverse functional fed by cross-fitted survival scores.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Track the second-order remainder of the composite map \((y,M,B)\mapsto yM_r^+B\) uniformly as the singular gap shrinks, and construct two local survival experiments when the derivative ceases to be regular.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weak-gap synthetic survival control, rank-robust pseudoinverse inference, and rank-selected censoring-robust panels found high-dimensional linear-functional results but no fixed-panel multi-block survival experiment.
adjacent_threads: Golub and Pereyra (1973), equation (4.12): the regular constant-rank derivative whose norm and remainder must be tracked as the gap closes.
Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024), Theorem 2: the regular orthogonal cell experiment that separates nuisance error from spectral nonregularity.
Han and Shah (2025), Theorem 2: the well-conditioned fixed-rank baseline without selected-rank inference.
seed_details.novelty_check: Choi, Kwon, and Liao require a high-dimensional low-rank matrix and a linear functional, whereas the proposed local experiment is fixed-dimensional and nonlinear in three noisy blocks. The gap/rank frontier remains unoccupied but is too risky to replace the regular theorem, so it is preserved as the first-class open question.
seed_details.referee_objection: Choi, Kwon, and Liao already solve inference under rank overestimation.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their diversified-projection correction uses both matrix dimensions growing and a linear target; neither its estimator nor its proof applies to a fixed-dimensional pseudoinverse map at a local singular-value collision.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The phase boundary is not guessed or assumed; it is left as a named open object to be derived by a local upper-bound and two-path lower-bound analysis.

seed_details.seed: Exact cancellation frontier for unadjusted Kaplan--Meier principal-component regression
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2312.00501, Introduction, Sections 3--4 on interpolation and survival-curve bias, equation (8), and Conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Curth et al. decompose bias from nonlinear survival models and show that synthetic individuals have distorted distributional spread, but they deliberately set aside the panel-cell Kaplan--Meier probability limit under covariate-dependent censoring. Their conclusion asks for more sophisticated survival-control corrections.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Derive every cell's marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-limit under conditional but not marginal independent censoring, substitute the resulting perturbations into \(y\), \(M\), and \(B\) simultaneously, and characterize the zero set of the resulting pseudoinverse bias map.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Kaplan--Meier/PCR cancellation and informative-censoring synthetic controls found separate Kaplan--Meier inconsistency and survival-control bias results, but no three-block necessary-and-sufficient cancellation formula.
adjacent_threads: Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024), Introduction and Theorem 1: the distinction between the marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-target and the covariate-standardized survival functional.
Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025), Section 2 and Corollary 2: deterministic minimum-norm PCR transport after taking probability limits.
Han and Shah (2025), Theorems 1--2: the exact true-curve donor-span relation and the naïve Kaplan--Meier spectral workflow.
seed_details.novelty_check: The neighboring papers separately establish Kaplan--Meier failure, PCR transport, and survival-control bias. None substitutes cell-specific pseudo-limits into the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post blocks simultaneously or identifies the exact cancellation zero set; the rational witness and continuity region therefore survive the scan.
seed_details.referee_objection: Kaplan--Meier inconsistency under dependent censoring is classical, so the conclusion is automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cellwise inconsistency need not survive the learned three-block transport because errors can cancel; the iff bias map and its relatively open nonzero region are the missing claims.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is not a single tuned counterexample: the rational law certifies nonemptiness, while continuity yields a relatively open subclass and the zero-bias exceptional set is characterized exactly.

seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2106.06602, Introduction, Theorem 2, Lemmas 4--7, proof of Theorem 2, and Concluding Remarks.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Westling et al. prove uniform asymptotic linearity in \(\ell^\infty([0,\tau])\) by a product-integral expansion, cross-fitting, and monotone-class entropy bounds. Their construction has no learned donor geometry.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Lift the finite-dimensional spectral derivative to a continuous operator on a product of c\`adl\`ag-function spaces and verify stochastic equicontinuity after donor transport.
seed_details.destination_search: Functional synthetic controls and uniform doubly robust survival inference exist separately; no censoring-robust spectral composition was located.
seed_details.referee_objection: With fixed pre-period weights, continuous-time post-period transport is only a bounded linear map of Westling et al.'s process.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection substantially lowers the incremental depth when the pre-fit grid stays fixed, so this seed is dropped in favor of the sharper fixed-grid three-block derivative.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because the strongest defensible version risks becoming a routine functional continuous-mapping corollary.

seed_details.seed: Semiparametric efficiency bound for a transported survival curve
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2106.06602, Theorem 1 and its pathwise-differentiability proof, Theorem 2, and Concluding Remarks.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Westling et al. identify the nonparametric efficient influence function for one marginal survival curve. On a product model of independent panel cells, the chain rule plausibly transports these efficient scores through a smooth fixed-rank map.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Form the product tangent space across cells and project the derivative of \(yM_r^+B\) onto it.
seed_details.destination_search: No published efficiency calculation for spectral survival control was found, but the product-model answer appears close to a direct chain-rule consequence.
seed_details.referee_objection: The efficiency bound is just the variance of the delta-method transport of already efficient cell scores.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds under independent cells and fixed dimensions, so efficiency is not retained as the headline kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped rather than promoting a routine semiparametric chain rule to a principal contribution.

seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2511.14133, Introduction, factor-model setup, Theorem 1, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Han and Shah impose a linear donor-span restriction on survival trajectories. Gunsilius instead identifies quantile barycenters in Wasserstein geometry, while Okano and Kurisu use isometric Hilbert embeddings; none of the opened papers gives correspondence conditions among these restrictions.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Characterize when one donor weight vector commutes with the survival-to-quantile transformation and the chosen Hilbert embedding, then construct separation models for necessity.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for equivalence of survival-function, quantile, and embedded synthetic controls found only the separate geometries.
seed_details.referee_objection: The geometries agree only in degenerate location families, making the theorem a taxonomy rather than an empirical method.
seed_details.rebuttal: A useful diagnostic may exist, but its estimable nondegenerate characterization is not yet supported by the current presolve evidence.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because feasibility and the TCL consumer are weaker than for censoring-robust inference.

seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Han and Shah target a single event-time survival curve. Their TCL endpoint combines death and treatment failure, while the paper does not separate competing cumulative-incidence functions.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the survival score by a cause-specific augmented-IPCW cumulative-incidence score before differentiating the same spectral map.
seed_details.destination_search: Lok et al. provide augmented-IPCW cumulative-incidence estimation, but no spectral panel transport; the transfer nevertheless appears structurally parallel to the selected kernel.
seed_details.referee_objection: Once the survival composition is proved, competing risks require only substituting another orthogonal cell score.
seed_details.rebuttal: The cause-specific score has additional nuisance structure, but the objection makes it a sequel rather than the first proposal.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped as a follow-on target rather than padded into the primary theorem package.

proposed_from.literature_map: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) identify and estimate a low-rank synthetic survival counterfactual using Kaplan--Meier cell curves under non-informative censoring; their Conclusion names IPCW as future work. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, Theorems 1--2 and Lemmas 4--7) derive the efficient survival score, its exact product-form remainder, cross-fitted pointwise and uniform asymptotic linearity, bands, and integrated contrasts under conditional censoring. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) characterize minimum-norm PCR and row-space out-of-sample transport, but not censoring-score limit theory. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) give the constant-rank Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse, including the two projector corrections. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) provide Gaussian multiplier and anti-concentration tools for maxima. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) diagnose survival-control distributional bias but do not characterize informative-censoring pseudo-limits inside all PCR blocks. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026, Theorem 3.1) obtain rank-robust inference for high-dimensional linear functionals by diversified projections; their regime and target do not subsume a fixed-panel pseudoinverse functional. Targeted searches through September 2026 found no closer paper containing the selected cell-score-plus-spectral-map composition.
